articles.title: Daylight Lands $80 Million for AI-Powered Security Operations
articles.snippet: Daylight Lands $80 Million for AI-Powered Security Operations SecurityWeek
articles.text:
Cybersecurity Funding
Daylight Lands $80 Million for AI-Powered Security Operations
The company plans to accelerate product development, hire new talent, expand its US presence, and enter new markets.
By
Ionut Arghire
|
November 12, 2026 (8:12 AM ET)
Flipboard
Reddit
Whatsapp
Whatsapp
Email
Israeli-American cybersecurity startup Daylight has raised $80 million in a Series B funding round that brings the total raised by the company to $120 million.
The investment round was led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives’ Growth Equity, with additional support from Okta Ventures, Bain Capital, Craft Ventures, Vintage Partners, and Maple Capital.
Founded in 2024, with headquarters in New York and Tel Aviv, Daylight has built Aura, an AI-native platform that hunts for, analyzes, and contains cyber threats in real time.
Combining AI automation with human expertise, the platform continuously builds, runs, and customizes agents that handle day-to-day operations based on customers’ workflows, risks, and priorities.
Daylight provides these capabilities as part of a flexible service model. Customers can select the service to be fully managed, co-managed, or supported by forward-deployed engineers.
As AI agents handle routine operations, customers can use Aura to investigate their security environments, access security data, and manage security operations.
Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.
Daylight also covers AI platforms that organizations use, offering protection against prompt injection, risky MCPs, and rogue AI-driven activity.
“As these agents become more capable, they’ll fundamentally change how threats are detected, investigated, and contained, with expert security engineers implementing, governing, and continuously improving their operations,” Daylight co-founder and CEO Hagai Shapira said.
“At Daylight, we’re already bringing this vision to life through an agent-native model that combines the speed and scale of AI with the judgment and oversight of human experts. We’re building the foundation for a new era of security operations,” Shapira added.
The company plans to use the fresh funding to accelerate its platform’s development, expand its security and technology teams, grow its presence in the US, and enter new markets in the EMEA and APAC regions.

articles.title: Course Corrected Raises €80 Million to Back European Energy and Resource Transition Startups
articles.snippet: Course Corrected Raises €80 Million to Back European Energy and Resource Transition Startups ESG Today
articles.text:
Energy Transition / Private Equity & Venture Capital
Course Corrected Raises €80 Million to Back European Energy and Resource Transition Startups
Kenny Fisher
November 12, 2026
Venture capital investor Course Corrected announced today that it has raised €80 million (USD$89 million) at the final close of its second fund, focused on investing in early-stage European technology companies across the energy and resource transition.
Founded in 2021 by Christine Ahlstrand, Kerstin Cooley and Katja Bergman, Stockholm-based Course Corrected invests in early-stage technology companies developing solutions to enable industries to become more energy, resource and cost efficient. Fund II builds on the firm’s first fund, which focused entirely on climate tech.
According to the firm, Fund II will invest in 20 – 30 companies across key themes including energy systems, industrial optimization and automation, electrification and resource-smart solutions, focusing on scalable businesses whose products advance the energy and resource transition.
Kerstin Cooley, founding partner at Course Corrected, said:
“We invest to generate strong financial returns. Impact is how we get there: by backing juggernauts that solve real problems, scale commercially, and transform industries for the better.”
Fund II invests only in European companies. Course Corrected noted that the fund’s close amidst a need for Europe to channel more of its savings into European businesses, noting that only a small fraction of pension and insurance assets are allocated to venture capital, and that more than half of EU venture funds’ investments are directed to startups outside of the EU.
Christine Ahlstrand, founding partner at Course Corrected, said:
“Europe has the research, the technology, the founders and the markets. But who will own the next generation of industry if we do not finance the companies building it?”
To date, Fund II has made seven investments, including Tavion, Renasens, eComID and Skye.
Investors in the fund include the European Investment Fund (EIF), which committed €35 million, Swedish state-owned venture capital investor Saminvest, pension investors SEB Life & Pension and SEB-Stiftelsen, a Swedish foundation and private investors.
Pontus Bergekrans, CIO at SEB Life & Pension AB, said:
“We believe Europe has the talent and innovation needed to lead the energy transition. Course Corrected combines a strong team, a focused strategy and access to companies addressing some of the region’s most important challenges.”

articles.text:
Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:27 AM
Eli Radiopharma: Nearly $60 Million Series A Financing To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline Toward Clinical Development
Eli Radiopharma has raised nearly $60 million (RMB 400 million) in Series A financing to advance its radiopharmaceutical pipeline toward clinical development. The funding will support preclinical research, regulatory submissions, early-stage clinical studies, and the expansion of the company’s research and development capabilities.
Huagai Capital led the financing round, with Bayland Capital serving as co-lead investor. Additional participants included Boyu Ventures, Delian Capital, InnoPinnacle Fund, Haibang Venture, Bairui Capital, Shenzhen Angel FOF Management, and Grand Flight Investment.
Existing shareholders CSPC & Growth Bio Fund, Huaige Capital, KHK Fund, Longfeng Venture, Hongsheng Capital, Bioclub Fund, and Skyfield Capital also participated in the financing.
Eli Radiopharma plans to allocate the proceeds toward preclinical research, investigational new drug applications, and early-stage clinical development. The company will also strengthen its research platforms, recruit additional talent, expand clinical operations, and pursue business development opportunities.
Founded in 2024, Eli Radiopharma focuses on developing radiopharmaceutical products that combine molecular targeting with radionuclide technology. Its pipeline includes diagnostic and therapeutic candidates designed to address unmet medical needs in oncology and neurological diseases.
The company has advanced multiple programs targeting novel molecular mechanisms through lead discovery, laboratory validation, and animal studies. Several candidates are approaching investigational new drug submissions, representing an important transition from early research toward human clinical testing.
Radiopharmaceuticals combine targeting molecules with radioactive isotopes to identify or treat diseased tissue. Therapeutic radioligands are designed to deliver radiation directly to tumors while limiting exposure to surrounding healthy tissue. Related diagnostic imaging agents can help physicians identify appropriate patients, evaluate disease progression, and monitor treatment responses.
The financing also reflects growing international interest in radiopharmaceutical innovation originating in China. Global pharmaceutical companies have increasingly explored opportunities involving novel molecular targets, therapeutic radionuclides, and expanded clinical applications.
Eli Radiopharma’s investors identified these areas as important drivers of future industry growth, particularly as radiopharmaceutical technologies move into additional cancer indications and other therapeutic applications.
The company’s longer-term strategy includes building a globally competitive pipeline capable of serving patients in international markets, including the U.S. and Europe. Its immediate priorities involve completing preclinical development, meeting regulatory requirements, and advancing differentiated candidates into clinical studies.
The Series A financing provides Eli Radiopharma with additional resources to move its lead programs closer to clinical validation while expanding the infrastructure needed to support a broader radiopharmaceutical development portfolio.

News provided by

Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital co-lead $30 million expansion to scale Kindo's go-to-market operations and accelerate development of its AI agent management platform
LOS ANGELES , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kindo , the run-anywhere AI agent management platform that puts the enterprise in control, today announced a $30 million raise co-led by Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, bringing total capital raised to $57.6 million. The company grew revenue by approximately 800% year over year in 2026 and will use the financing to expand its go-to-market organization and accelerate development of its enterprise AI Control Center and Deep Hat models and add-ons.
Continue Reading
Meet Kindo video
As autonomous agents spread through the enterprise and their numbers swell into the thousands, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams struggle to control risks and costs without a centralized tool that can discover, observe, and control the entire enterprise AI footprint. Every time a company lets an AI agent access data, update a customer record, approve a request, or change a production system, it delegates authority. The same permissions that let an agent get work done can let it expose sensitive data, make changes outside company policy, disrupt a critical workflow, or rack up huge inference costs.
"Agent builders from the AI labs, hyperscalers, and thousands of startups make it easy to deploy powerful agents across the business," said Ron Williams, founder and CEO of Kindo. "What's missing is the tooling that lets an organization centrally control how those agents are built, what data they can reach, where that data can go, and what they cost, while also allowing support teams to reach in and fix an agent at any hour. That gap is why the teams responsible for supporting and controlling Al are rightfully putting the brakes on Al transformation."
Kindo gives organizations control of the AI agents already running across their operations. It starts with discovery, uncovering shadow AI and mapping where agents are in use, then brings their activity, access, costs, and outcomes into one view. The teams that must support and control AI, IT, Security, Finance, and Compliance, get a single set of controls: what employees can do with an agent, what an agent can touch, how it behaves around the clock, and what it costs. The result is an AI Operations Center, SOC- and NOC-style monitoring and intervention for AI, where those teams eliminate risk, drive down cost, and make sure AI delivers measurable outcomes.
Implementation is turnkey and is run by the IT operations staff an organization already has. Teams connect the agents, data sources, and AI models already in use, and from that moment everything is discovered, observed, and controlled from one place. Kindo's gateways govern and audit every call an agent makes to connected data, tools, and approved models. Identity controls apply the organization's existing permissions to people and agents alike, with the option to tighten them centrally. For mission-critical agents that need deeper control, Kindo's harness, purpose-built for centralized agent operations, adds around-the-clock monitoring, support, and direct intervention, including the ability to take over an agent when something goes wrong.

articles.text:
Charta Health: $55 Million Series B To Expand AI Medical Chart Review
By Amit Chowdhry
Nov 11, 2026
Charta Health: $55 Million Series B To Expand AI Medical Chart Review
Charta Health has raised $55 million in Series B funding to expand its artificial intelligence platform for medical chart review and create a common standard of billing accuracy for healthcare providers and insurers. Insight Partners led the round, with participation from existing investors Madrona, Bain Capital Ventures, and South Park Commons, along with QuantumLight.
Charta applies AI to unstructured clinical information, including physician notes, scanned orders, laboratory results, and images. Its technology reviews medical records to determine whether documented care supports the codes used for billing.
The company wants providers and payers to resolve coding discrepancies before a claim is submitted rather than through denials, audits, and appeals. Those administrative processes contribute billions of dollars in costs to the U.S. healthcare system.
Charta for Providers reviews every chart before billing and checks the documentation against official coding guidance, payer rules, and an organization’s clinical protocols. Findings are presented within electronic health record workflows for human approval.
The company says its platform produces consistent double-digit reductions in denial rates. It also gives compliance and medical leadership teams information about documentation gaps, recurring errors, and provider performance.
Charta works with healthcare organizations including American Family Care, Grow Therapy, and Pediatric Associates Family of Companies. It will use the funding to improve the accuracy and intelligence of its provider technology and expand into additional medical specialties.
The financing also supports Charta for Payers, a suite developed with one of the country’s largest health insurers. The offering initially focuses on Medicare Advantage and Affordable Care Act Marketplace plans.
Its six products cover retrospective hierarchical condition category coding, automated second-pass reviews, coder workflows, prospective risk-adjustment intelligence, audit preparation, and quality care-gap detection.
The technology can identify conditions documented but not coded and diagnoses that lack sufficient clinical support. Charta’s longer-term objective is to give providers and insurers a consistent interpretation of the same medical record before reimbursement decisions are made.
KEY QUOTE:
“Healthcare payments depend on the medical chart, and charting errors cause costly problems across the entire process. As payers and providers both adopt AI, we believe the opportunity lies in getting the underlying record, or the ‘ground truth,’ right before a claim is submitted. Charta pairs AI with customer-specific coding expertise and serves both sides of that market. We are excited to partner with Justin, Scott, and the team as they scale.”
Jeff Horing, Co-Founder and Managing Director at Insight Partners
